DocumentInfo.TITLE: Speech: Donald Trump in Columbus, OH - October 13, 2016
DocumentInfo.SPEAKER: Donald Trump

Paragraph.text: Thank you. I am so happy to be back here in Columbus. Make sure you request your absentee ballot to vote by mail. And remind your friends and family to do the same. We are now 26 days away from the most important election of our lifetimes. And we've only begun to fight. If we win, we will create a booming and thriving economy for young Americans. We will create safe communities, lower taxes, leaner government, affordable childcare and healthcare, and a government that is honest and decent and fair.

Paragraph.text: We are the campaign of change. We will deliver jobs, opportunity and justice for future generations. I've wanted this race to be about the issues. But the Clinton Campaign has refused to discuss the issues.

Paragraph.text: First, we will Lower the Cost of College and Solve the Student Loan Crisis. Tuition at public four-year institutions was 40% higher in the last school year than it was ten years ago. In all, Americans owe $1.3 trillion on their student loans -- more than auto loans, credit card debt, or home equity loans nationwide. Students should not be asked to pay more on their loans than they can afford, and the debt should not be an albatross around their necks for the rest of their lives.

Paragraph.text: That is why under my student loan program, we would cap repayment to an affordable portion of a borrower's income -- 12.5%. And if borrowers work hard and make their full payments for 15 years, we will let them get on with their lives. That's the nature of the deal we give many public employees today. Every American deserves the same deal, so we will equalize treatment so everyone can start saving for their families and retirement by the time they are 15 years out of college.

Paragraph.text: In addition, I will take steps to push colleges to cut the skyrocketing cost of tuition. If the federal government is going to subsidize student loans, it has a right to expect that colleges work hard to control costs and invest their resources in their students.

Some schools are paying more to hedge funds and private equity managers than they are spending on tuition assistance -- while taxpayers are guaranteeing hundreds of billions of dollars of student loans to pay for rising tuition.

Paragraph.text: We want universities to spend their endowments on their students, not themselves. They need to use that money to cut the college debt and college tuition. According to the Department of Education, the number of college administrators is up more than 60 percent since 1993 -- ten times the increase in tenured faculty positions.

I will also make it a priority to protect students' rights to free speech on campus.

Paragraph.text: And we must hold all schools equally accountable for their performance. I will make sure that students have the information they need about all of their options before starting school, and for repaying their student loans upon leaving school. There is a lot of room for improvement in this regard. Currently, students navigate 16 complex repayment plans, 8 forgiveness programs, and 32 deferment and forbearance options -- each of these programs has their own nuances and qualifications.
